claim: In Q2 FY2026, Apple's board authorized an ADDITIONAL $100 billion share repurchase program on top of existing authorization, alongside a 4% dividend increase to $0.27/share.
stance_target: Shareholder returns (buybacks) remain a first-order lever for total return independent of fundamental growth, per the 2-5y total-return decomposition identity
scope_conditions: Announced with Q2 FY2026 results (quarter ended March 28, 2026)
quoted_support: The board of directors has also authorized an additional program to repurchase up to $100 billion of the Company's common stock.

claim: Q2 FY2026 iPhone revenue grew 21.7% YoY to $56,994M, a March-quarter record, explicitly attributed by Apple to 'extraordinary demand for the iPhone 17 lineup', while Services grew a slower 16.3% YoY to $30,976M.
stance_target: Whether an AI-driven or design-driven iPhone upgrade supercycle can plausibly reset the replacement cycle
scope_conditions: Q2 FY2026 only, single data point of a broader multi-quarter cycle
quoted_support: iPhone achieved a March quarter revenue record, fueled by such extraordinary demand for the iPhone 17 lineup.

claim: Greater China revenue accelerated to $20,497M in Q2 FY2026, up 28.1% YoY, the second consecutive quarter of >20% China growth in FY2026.
stance_target: Structural, ongoing China revenue decline as a base-case bear thesis
quoted_support: Greater China 20,497 / 16,002 (three months ended March 28, 2026 / March 29, 2025)

claim: Apple's Q2 FY2026 Services gross margin (76.7%) is roughly double the Products gross margin (38.7%), consistent across all three FY2026 quarters observed.
stance_target: Services deserves a materially higher multiple than Products on a durability/profitability basis
scope_conditions: Q2 FY2026, three months ended March 28, 2026
